name: tear-ticket
title: Tear Ticket
description: A boarding-pass style ticket with a photo header, trip details and a perforated stub. Moving the mouse tips it in perspective; dragging the stub pulls thin fibres until it rips away and tumbles off.
use: A ticket, voucher or pass benefits from a tactile reveal that marks it used, not just a checkbox.
avoid: Dragging is pointer-only, the tear needs motion to land, and it suits one-off tickets rather than long lists.
a11y: The stub is a labelled button and Enter tears it, but there is no visible focus ring on it. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A wide rounded ticket in dark grey, a mountain photo across the top under the route line, three labelled details beneath and a dotted perforation separating a narrow stub that shows the seat.
behaves: The card leans toward the pointer in a soft 3D tilt, with the photo and text shifting at slightly different depths. Dragging the stub pulls thin fibres across the perforation until they snap and the stub falls away.
customise: Width, height, stub size, image, body children, stub slot, background, border, tilt strength and tear feel are props; the tear simulation is fixed.
weight: moderate: Springs follow the pointer and a hand-written loop runs only while tearing.
